question: With reference to the RBI's record surplus transfer of Rs 2.87 lakh crore to the Centre for FY26, consider the following statements:
statements: It is the highest-ever surplus transfer made by the RBI.
The transferable surplus is decided under the Economic Capital Framework, based on the Bimal Jalan Committee's recommendations.
This surplus is automatically shared with the States through the divisible pool under the Finance Commission's formula.
explanation: Rs 2.87 lakh crore is the highest-ever transfer, decided via the Economic Capital Framework (Bimal Jalan Committee). It is non-tax revenue outside the divisible pool, so States get no automatic share (statement 3 wrong).
subject: Current Affairs

question: The National Statistical Commission (NSC), reconstituted in June 2026, is best described as a:

options.text: Statutory body created under an Act of Parliament
Non-statutory, non-constitutional body set up by an executive resolution
Body established under Article 338 of the Constitution

explanation: The NSC is a non-statutory, non-constitutional advisory body set up by an executive resolution (1999) — a frequent Prelims trap.
subject: Current Affairs

question: With reference to the Reciprocal Exchange of Logistics Agreement (RELOS), operationalised in June 2026, consider the following statements:
statements: It is a logistics-support agreement between India and Russia.
It allows either country to establish permanent military bases on the other's territory.
It belongs to the same family of agreements as LEMOA, signed by India with the United States.
explanation: RELOS is an India–Russia logistics-sharing pact, of the LEMOA/ACSA family; it is non-basing (no permanent foreign bases), so statement 2 is wrong.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Consider the following statements regarding El Niño / ENSO, in the news in June 2026:
statements: NOAA issued an El Niño Advisory, with conditions expected to strengthen into the winter of 2026–27.
El Niño is generally associated with the suppression of the Indian southwest monsoon.
The "Southern Oscillation" refers to the see-saw of atmospheric pressure between the eastern and western tropical Pacific.
explanation: All three correct: NOAA's El Niño Advisory (June 2026), monsoon suppression over India, and the Southern Oscillation as the east–west tropical-Pacific pressure see-saw.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), in news in June 2026:

options.text: Is scheduled to enter into force on 15 July 2026, alongside the Double Contribution Convention (DCC)
Is India's first-ever free trade agreement with any country
Can be implemented only after ratification by the WTO

explanation: India–UK CETA enters into force 15 July 2026, alongside the Double Contribution Convention (DCC); the UK eliminates duties on ~99% of Indian tariff lines.
subject: Current Affairs

question: With reference to the eight Ladakh handicraft products granted GI tags in June 2026, consider the following:
statements: Geographical Indications in India are registered under the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999.
A registered GI is valid for 10 years and is renewable.
India's first GI tag was granted to Darjeeling Tea.
explanation: All three correct: GI Act, 1999; 10-year renewable validity; India's first GI was Darjeeling Tea (2004).
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Money Restoration Module (MRM) and the Grievance Redressal Mechanism (GRM), launched in 2026 to help cyber-fraud victims, are initiatives of the:

options.text: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs
CERT-In under the Ministry of Electronics and IT
National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC)

explanation: MRM and GRM are run by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the MHA; MRM lets victims reclaim up to Rs 50,000.
subject: Current Affairs

question: With reference to ship recycling, in news in June 2026, consider the following:
statements: Per UNCTAD's *Review of Maritime Transport 2025*, India became the world's No.1 ship-recycling nation in 2025.
India's principal ship-recycling hub is at Alang, Gujarat.
India's domestic law giving effect to the Hong Kong Convention is the Recycling of Ships Act, 2019.
explanation: All three correct: UNCTAD ranks India No.1 (35.4% share, 2025); hub at Alang, Gujarat; Recycling of Ships Act, 2019 gives effect to the Hong Kong Convention.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Regarding the two expert panels central to the Western Ghats Eco-Sensitive Area question, consider the following:
statements: The Gadgil Committee (WGEEP, 2011) recommended that the entire Western Ghats be treated as an Ecologically Sensitive Area.
The Kasturirangan Committee (HLWG, 2013) recommended that about 37% of the Western Ghats be designated as ESA.
ESAs in the Western Ghats are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
explanation: All three correct: Gadgil (2011) = entire Ghats as ESA (~1,29,037 sq km); Kasturirangan (2013) = ~37% (~60,000 sq km); ESAs notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Consider the following statements regarding India and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), in news in June 2026:
statements: India secured the FATF Vice-Presidency for the first time.
FATF is headquartered in Paris.
India became a member of FATF in 2010.
explanation: All three correct: India won the FATF Vice-Presidency for the first time (Vivek Aggarwal, 2026–27 term); FATF is Paris-based; India joined in 2010.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Fibre-optic drones, recently in the news, are valued in modern warfare mainly because they:

options.text: Are immune to radio-frequency jamming and spoofing, being controlled through a physical fibre-optic cable
Are powered by compact onboard nuclear reactors
Rely on a satellite-navigation link that cannot be intercepted

explanation: A physical fibre-optic cable carries commands/video by light pulses, emitting almost no RF → immune to jamming/spoofing (limitation: cable caps range and can break).
subject: Current Affairs

question: Rakhigarhi, in news in June 2026 for the transfer of skeletal remains to the Anthropological Survey of India for ancient-DNA study, is:

options.text: An early Buddhist site in Madhya Pradesh
A Chalukyan temple complex in Karnataka

explanation: Rakhigarhi (Haryana) is among the largest Harappan (Indus–Saraswati) sites; remains went to AnSI, Kolkata, for ancient-DNA study. Part B — Modern History
subject: Current Affairs

question: The major outbreak of the Revolt of 1857 began on 10 May 1857 at:
explanation: The major outbreak began at Meerut on 10 May 1857. (Mangal Pandey's earlier individual revolt was at Barrackpore, 29 March 1857.)
subject: Modern History

question: With reference to the Partition of Bengal, consider the following statements:
statements: It was carried out in 1905 during the viceroyalty of Lord Curzon.
It triggered the Swadeshi and Boycott movement.
The partition was annulled in 1911.
explanation: All correct: Partitioned in 1905 under Curzon, sparking the Swadeshi movement; annulled in 1911.
subject: Modern History

question: The first session of the Indian National Congress (1885) was:

options.text: Held at Bombay and presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee
Held at Calcutta and presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji
Held at Madras and presided over by A.O. Hume
Held at Allahabad and presided over by Surendranath Banerjee

explanation: First INC session: Bombay, 1885, presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee (founded with A.O. Hume's help).
subject: Modern History

question: Arrange the following Gandhian movements in correct chronological order:
statements: Kheda Satyagraha
Champaran Satyagraha
Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha)
Quit India Movement
explanation: Champaran (1917) → Kheda (1918) → Dandi (1930) → Quit India (1942) = 2 – 1 – 3 – 4.
subject: Modern History

question: Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced for the first time by which of the following?
explanation: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced by the Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms).
subject: Modern History

question: The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875 by:
explanation: The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875 by Swami Dayananda Saraswati ("Back to the Vedas"; *Satyarth Prakash*).
subject: Modern History

question: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the resolution of "Purna Swaraj" (complete independence) adopted, with 26 January 1930 to be observed as Independence Day?

options.text: Lahore Session, 1929 (presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru)
Calcutta Session, 1928 (presided over by Motilal Nehru)
Karachi Session, 1931 (presided over by Sardar Patel)
Lucknow Session, 1916 (presided over by A.C. Mazumdar)

explanation: The Purna Swaraj resolution was adopted at the Lahore Session, 1929 (presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru); 26 Jan 1930 was observed as Independence Day.
subject: Modern History
